transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up time from people who need it more, honestly. It's probably nothing too serious, but... well, I came in because I just seem to be worrying about everything lately. 

And I mean everything. My real estate clients, the state of the housing market, my family, money... even just, you know, whether moving to my new condo was the right decision. I know everyone stresses out sometimes, and I don't want to sound dramatic, but it just feels a little out of proportion to what is actually happening. Does that make sense? I just wanted to check if that's normal, or if I'm doing the right thing by being here.
Have you experienced any episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?

Oh, no, I don't think so. Um, nothing like a sudden, intense fear like you're describing. It's really just... more of a constant, quiet worry in the background, if that makes sense? Never anything that sudden or extreme. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I'm certainly glad I haven't had anything like that, but I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions correctly. Am I giving you the right kind of information?
Have you been avoiding any activities or situations because of your worries?

No, no, I wouldn't say I'm avoiding things. I mean, I still go to work, I still show houses, I still see my family. I try my best to keep up with everything, I really do. I don't want to let anyone down or, you know, seem like I can't handle my responsibilities. 

Sometimes I might... hesitate a little before making a big phone call, or I might double-check my schedule a few more times than I need to, just to be sure. But I always get it done. I hope that's okay? I just try to push through it, because I know people are relying on me. Does that sound like I'm handling it alright?
Have you experienced any traumatic events in the past?

Oh, no... no, thankfully. I've been very lucky in that regard. I know some people go through just awful things, and I haven't had to deal with anything like that. Just the normal ups and downs of life, you know? Nothing I would ever call traumatic. 

Honestly, it makes me feel a little silly being here for just... worrying, especially when I know how much worse other people have it. I really don't have any major past trauma to point to. But, um, I hope that's helpful for you to know? Am I giving you the right details so far?
Have you noticed any changes in your physical health, such as headaches or difficulty sleeping?

Well, physical health... I mean, I feel mostly fine. I don't really get headaches or anything like that. I try to take good care of myself. 

With sleeping, um... I guess it could be a little better? I do make sure to get into bed at a reasonable hour every night. I know how important that is. It's just that sometimes, my mind gets a little busy. I start thinking about, you know, condo fees, or the showings I have the next day, or I'll wonder if I missed a detail in a client's contract. Just silly work things. 

So it can take me a little while to finally settle down and drift off. And then, I suppose I do wake up feeling like I haven't quite rested as much as I should have. But I'm sure that's just a normal part of getting older and having a busy job, right? It's not terrible, I still get up and go to work. I hope that's the kind of thing you're asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Is this worry present most of the time, for more days than not, over the past few months?

Well, um... yes, I suppose it has been going on for a little while. Not that it's taking over my life or anything, I'm still functioning perfectly fine. But, yes, it's been pretty consistent. 

I guess... if I really think about it, it started around a year and two months ago. That was right after I sold the house I'd lived in for years and downsized into my condo. It was a good move, a very sensible decision, really. Just, you know, a big adjustment. I think my mind just sort of got into this habit of worrying during all that transition, and it hasn't quite stopped. 

But it's not every single second of the day! Just... more days than not, like you said. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. Does that timeline make sense for what you usually see? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Has your worry been interfering with your relationships or daily activities in any way?

Well, um... my relationships are fine, really. I still see my friends and family, and I always try to be present for them. I wouldn't say the worry gets in the way of that. 

As for my daily activities, like work... I mean, I'm still getting everything done! I haven't dropped the ball on anything major. It's just... well, maybe things are taking me a little longer than they used to. Even just straightforward things, like, um, listing negotiations or reviewing a standard contract. I find myself reading them over and over, just to be absolutely sure I haven't missed a single detail. 

And, I suppose I have been delaying returning some client calls here and there. Not because I don't want to talk to them! Just because... I want to make sure I've checked everything perfectly before I give them an update. I don't feel quite as confident until I've double and triple-checked. It's just me wanting to do a good job for my clients, you know? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm doing poorly at work, because I really am trying my best. Is it normal to be a little extra cautious like that?
Would you say that your worry is causing you significant distress?

Distress? Oh, um... no, I really wouldn't use a word quite that strong. "Distress" makes it sound so... well, severe, doesn't it? Like I'm falling apart or completely overwhelmed, and I promise I'm definitely not doing that. 

I'm managing everything just fine, really. It's more of a... I guess a mild nuisance sometimes? Just a little bothersome background noise when I'm trying to relax. But I can still smile and enjoy my day, and I always try to keep a positive attitude about things. 

I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm sitting around pulling my hair out or anything, because I'm really quite okay overall. Is it alright if I just describe it as a bit of an annoyance?
Would you say your worry has affected your performance at work or your ability to take on new responsibilities?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say it's really affected my performance. Like I mentioned before, I'm still getting everything done, and my clients are very well taken care of. I pride myself on being a good agent, and I certainly wouldn't let a little extra worrying stop me from doing my job well. 

As for new responsibilities... well, I suppose I haven't been actively seeking out a lot of new listings lately. But that's just because the market is a bit unpredictable right now, and I want to make sure I'm giving my full, undivided attention to the clients I already have. It's just a strategic choice, really, to focus on quality over quantity. 

I'm definitely still capable of taking on more if I needed to, though! I just... I like to make sure everything is perfectly in order before I add to my plate. That's just being a responsible professional, don't you think? I hope that doesn't make it seem like I'm not capable, because I really am.
Are there any small, everyday things that you avoid doing because of your worries?

Oh, avoid things? Goodness, no. I really don't think I avoid anything at all. 

I mean, I still do all the normal things—grocery shopping, running errands, keeping the house tidy. I certainly wouldn't let a little worry stop me from living my life or taking care of my responsibilities. I'm very proactive about my day-to-day tasks. 

I suppose sometimes I might... well, if I'm not entirely sure about something, I might just wait a little bit before making a decision. Like, maybe I won't buy a certain household item right away until I've checked a few different stores to make sure I'm getting the best quality. But that's not avoiding, right? That's just being a smart shopper! 

I really do try to handle everything that comes my way. I hope that shows that I'm still functioning perfectly well, doesn't it?
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Restless? On edge? Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. Those words make it sound like I'm pacing the floors or snapping at people, and I promise I'm really quite even-keeled! 

I mean, I suppose everyone gets a little... energized sometimes, right? Like when you have a lot on your plate and you just want to make sure everything is handled properly. Sometimes I might feel a little burst of nervous energy, just wanting to stay on top of things. But I wouldn't call it being "on edge." It's more just being alert and ready for the day. 

I always try to stay pleasant and calm, especially with my clients. I hope you don't think I'm sitting around jittery all day, because I really do keep it together quite nicely. Does that sound like a normal amount of energy to you?
Do you often feel tense in your muscles?

Tense? Oh, well... I suppose everyone carries a little tension, don't they? It's just part of being a professional and working hard. 

I wouldn't say I'm walking around completely stiff or anything like that. But, um, I do notice that by the end of the day, my neck and shoulders can feel a bit... tight. Just like I've been bracing myself a little, you know? And, well, sometimes if I'm driving between listings or just sitting at my desk going over paperwork, I'll catch myself clenching my jaw just a tiny bit. 

But I'm sure that's just normal stress from a busy day, right? It's nothing a nice warm bath in the evening can't fix. I really try to take good care of myself so it doesn't become a problem. That's a perfectly normal way to carry a little stress, isn't it?
Is your worry usually about one specific thing or many different things?

One specific thing? Oh, um... well, I suppose that's actually sort of why I decided to come in and speak with you. I don't want to sound like a complainer, I promise, but it does seem like my mind has been jumping to... quite a few different things lately. 

It's not just one big issue. I seem to be worrying about, well, almost everything now. My clients, the real estate market—which is just part of being a good agent, of course! But then I also catch myself fretting over my family, and money, and... even things like whether moving to the condo was the right decision. 

I try so hard to keep a good perspective on it all, but sometimes it just feels a little out of proportion to what's actually happening in reality. Like I'm making mountains out of molehills, you know? I'm usually so capable of managing my thoughts and keeping a positive attitude. I hope I don't sound completely unreasonable, do I? It's just a lot to juggle all at once.
Do you feel like you're able to control your worrying most of the time?

Control it? Oh, well... I try, I really do. I mean, I'm usually very good at managing my time and my thoughts. But lately... um, to be completely honest, it feels a little harder than it should be. 

I try to just brush it off. I'll tell myself, "Parin, this isn't urgent, just put it aside for now." And I really mean to! But then... well, one little concern sort of just leads right into another. And before I even realize what's happening, I've spent, oh, maybe half an hour just replaying all these tiny little details in my head that I fully intended to just let go of. 

I know it sounds a bit silly, getting caught up like that. I really am trying my best to keep it all in check. I just... I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything, because I'm still getting my work done! It's just a little harder to steer my mind away once it starts going. Is that... is that something other people struggle with sometimes?
Do you find yourself worrying about everyday, mundane tasks or responsibilities, such as household chores or meal planning?

Everyday chores? Oh, no, thankfully not. I mean... I'm actually quite organized when it comes to the house. 

I don't want you to think I'm just completely overwhelmed by every little thing in my life! I still keep the condo very tidy, and meals are, well, they're just part of the normal routine. I've always prided myself on keeping a nice home, especially being in real estate. 

It's really just those bigger things we talked about—my clients, the market, my family—that seem to get my mind racing. But the laundry and the grocery shopping? No, I handle all of that just fine without a second thought. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I'm still keeping up with all my normal, day-to-day responsibilities perfectly well?
Do you worry about being judged or evaluated by others in social situations?

Oh, being judged? Um... no, actually. I don't think I worry about that at all. In my line of work, you really have to be a people person, you know? I'm always meeting new clients, hosting open houses, and going to community events. I actually quite enjoy all of that! 

I've always been very comfortable chatting with people and making connections. I don't really sit around worrying about what they think of me socially. I mean, I want them to think I'm a competent agent, of course! But just in regular social situations... no, I feel quite confident there. That's a good thing, right? That I still have that confidence when I'm out and about with people?
Do you find yourself putting off decisions or tasks because of your worries?

Well, putting things off... I wouldn't say I'm procrastinating, exactly. I've always prided myself on being very prompt and professional! But, um... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, I have noticed that I'm taking a bit more time with certain things at work lately. Just to be thorough, you know? 

Like, even with very straightforward listing negotiations or just standard contract reviews... they seem to be taking me quite a bit longer than they used to. And I have... well, I've had to delay returning a few phone calls here and there. Not because I'm ignoring anyone, I promise! I just... I haven't been feeling completely confident that I’ve checked everything carefully enough before I speak to them. I end up needing to look over the paperwork a few extra times just to be absolutely sure I haven't missed a single detail. 

I just want to make sure everything is perfect for my clients. That's just being a responsible agent, right? It's perfectly normal to want to double-check your work like that?
Do you feel like your worry is something that you can't seem to shake off, even when things are going well?

Well, I... I try very hard to just brush it off, especially when I know there's no real problem. I really do try to just stay positive. 

But, um... yes, I suppose sometimes it is a little hard to just let it go. Even when I tell myself, 'Parin, this is not urgent, everything is fine,' it just... well, one little concern seems to lead to another. And then, before I even realize it, I've spent half an hour just replaying all these small details in my head that I really meant to just put aside. 

I'm sure everyone does that sometimes, though, right? Just getting a little caught up in the details when you want to do a good job? It doesn't mean I'm falling apart or anything! I just... I care a lot about getting things right. That's a good quality to have, isn't it?
Do you worry about things that most people would consider minor or insignificant?

Minor things? Um... well, I wouldn't call them insignificant, exactly. They are important parts of life! But... I suppose, yes, that is actually why I finally came in to see you. 

I just seem to worry about, well, absolutely everything now. It's not just the contracts at work. It's my clients, the state of the housing market, my family, money... I even catch myself agonizing over whether moving to the condo was the right decision. And I know, logically, that it feels completely out of proportion to what is actually happening in reality. 

I feel a bit foolish even saying it out loud, to be honest. It's perfectly normal to care about your family and your future, right? I just... I suppose I'm just letting all these thoughts get a bit bigger than they need to be lately. That's a very common thing for people to go through, isn't it?
Is your worry usually focused on one specific area of your life, such as work or family?

Well, um... like I was just saying, I don't think it's just one specific thing. I really wish it was! It would probably be much easier to handle if it just stayed at the office, you know? 

But no, it kind of... it just hops around from work to my family, to the house... just whatever happens to be on my plate that day. I try my best not to let it overwhelm me, of course! I've always been very good at juggling different responsibilities. It's just that lately, the worrying kind of tags along with whatever it is I'm doing. 

I hope I'm not making myself sound like a complete mess! I really do keep things running smoothly most of the time. It's fairly typical for women my age to just have a lot on their minds across the board, wouldn't you say?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the worry is about one specific thing or many different things. This maps to Excessive_Anxiety_Worry, which describes worry occurring persistently about a number of events or activities (e.g., clients, the market, family, money, condo decision).

patient.answer:
One specific thing? Oh, um... well, I suppose that's actually sort of why I decided to come in and speak with you. I don't want to sound like a complainer, I promise, but it does seem like my mind has been jumping to... quite a few different things lately. 

It's not just one big issue. I seem to be worrying about, well, almost everything now. My clients, the real estate market—which is just part of being a good agent, of course! But then I also catch myself fretting over my family, and money, and... even things like whether moving to the condo was the right decision. 

I try so hard to keep a good perspective on it all, but sometimes it just feels a little out of proportion to what's actually happening in reality. Like I'm making mountains out of molehills, you know? I'm usually so capable of managing my thoughts and keeping a positive attitude. I hope I don't sound completely unreasonable, do I? It's just a lot to juggle all at once.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's worry is excessive and uncontrollable
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're able to control your worrying most of the time?

target_item.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
target_item.manifestation: Even when I tell myself, 'Parin, this is not urgent,' one concern leads to another, and before I know it I’ve spent half an hour replaying small details I meant to let go.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient is able to control their worrying, which directly corresponds to the symptom Uncontrollable_Worry (S057).

patient.answer:
Control it? Oh, well... I try, I really do. I mean, I'm usually very good at managing my time and my thoughts. But lately... um, to be completely honest, it feels a little harder than it should be. 

I try to just brush it off. I'll tell myself, "Parin, this isn't urgent, just put it aside for now." And I really mean to! But then... well, one little concern sort of just leads right into another. And before I even realize what's happening, I've spent, oh, maybe half an hour just replaying all these tiny little details in my head that I fully intended to just let go of. 

I know it sounds a bit silly, getting caught up like that. I really am trying my best to keep it all in check. I just... I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything, because I'm still getting my work done! It's just a little harder to steer my mind away once it starts going. Is that... is that something other people struggle with sometimes?

patient.answer:
Everyday chores? Oh, no, thankfully not. I mean... I'm actually quite organized when it comes to the house. 

I don't want you to think I'm just completely overwhelmed by every little thing in my life! I still keep the condo very tidy, and meals are, well, they're just part of the normal routine. I've always prided myself on keeping a nice home, especially being in real estate. 

It's really just those bigger things we talked about—my clients, the market, my family—that seem to get my mind racing. But the laundry and the grocery shopping? No, I handle all of that just fine without a second thought. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I'm still keeping up with all my normal, day-to-day responsibilities perfectly well?

doctor.intent: determine the presence of anxiety symptoms in social interactions
doctor.question: Do you worry about being judged or evaluated by others in social situations?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about social anxiety (worrying about being judged or evaluated by others in social situations), which is a symptom of Social Anxiety Disorder. My symptom profile does not include social anxiety.

patient.answer:
Oh, being judged? Um... no, actually. I don't think I worry about that at all. In my line of work, you really have to be a people person, you know? I'm always meeting new clients, hosting open houses, and going to community events. I actually quite enjoy all of that! 

I've always been very comfortable chatting with people and making connections. I don't really sit around worrying about what they think of me socially. I mean, I want them to think I'm a competent agent, of course! But just in regular social situations... no, I feel quite confident there. That's a good thing, right? That I still have that confidence when I'm out and about with people?

doctor.intent: Determine the level of avoidance behavior
doctor.question: Do you find yourself putting off decisions or tasks because of your worries?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment

patient.answer:
Well, putting things off... I wouldn't say I'm procrastinating, exactly. I've always prided myself on being very prompt and professional! But, um... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, I have noticed that I'm taking a bit more time with certain things at work lately. Just to be thorough, you know? 

Like, even with very straightforward listing negotiations or just standard contract reviews... they seem to be taking me quite a bit longer than they used to. And I have... well, I've had to delay returning a few phone calls here and there. Not because I'm ignoring anyone, I promise! I just... I haven't been feeling completely confident that I’ve checked everything carefully enough before I speak to them. I end up needing to look over the paperwork a few extra times just to be absolutely sure I haven't missed a single detail. 

I just want to make sure everything is perfect for my clients. That's just being a responsible agent, right? It's perfectly normal to want to double-check your work like that?

Well, I... I try very hard to just brush it off, especially when I know there's no real problem. I really do try to just stay positive. 

But, um... yes, I suppose sometimes it is a little hard to just let it go. Even when I tell myself, 'Parin, this is not urgent, everything is fine,' it just... well, one little concern seems to lead to another. And then, before I even realize it, I've spent half an hour just replaying all these small details in my head that I really meant to just put aside. 

I'm sure everyone does that sometimes, though, right? Just getting a little caught up in the details when you want to do a good job? It doesn't mean I'm falling apart or anything! I just... I care a lot about getting things right. That's a good quality to have, isn't it?

Minor things? Um... well, I wouldn't call them insignificant, exactly. They are important parts of life! But... I suppose, yes, that is actually why I finally came in to see you.

I feel a bit foolish even saying it out loud, to be honest. It's perfectly normal to care about your family and your future, right? I just... I suppose I'm just letting all these thoughts get a bit bigger than they need to be lately. That's a very common thing for people to go through, isn't it?

Well, um... like I was just saying, I don't think it's just one specific thing. I really wish it was! It would probably be much easier to handle if it just stayed at the office, you know?

I hope I'm not making myself sound like a complete mess! I really do keep things running smoothly most of the time. It's fairly typical for women my age to just have a lot on their minds across the board, wouldn't you say?
